statement: The integration report retains resolution: it does not pile every declared system against full satisfaction, and it reads enough systems for the measurement to mean anything.
rationale: This is H006's ceiling-saturation check pointed at the new layer, and it is here so that the architecture layer can fail in the way the per-entry layer already can. A report that has only ever returned full satisfaction cannot distinguish an integrated system from an unchecked one, and a layer added without a test that can refuse it is a layer that will confirm whatever it is given. The same reasoning H006's revision records applies: a high satisfaction rate over a set someone assembled is the expected result of assembling it, and running out of resolution is the defect that measures.
prediction: At least two systems report a runs_on fraction, at most half of them sit at full satisfaction, and the spread between highest and lowest is at least 0.2.

measures.target: whether the integration report discriminates between assemblies
measures.rendering: ceiling saturation and spread over the runs_on fractions the report produces
measures.target_question: Does the integration report discriminate between assemblies, or does it only describe the one set that has been declared so far?

last_result.summary: 1 evaluable system(s), below the 2 needed for saturation to mean anything — with one reading the spread is zero by construction; 1/1 systems report full satisfaction — the report cannot tell an integrated system from an unchecked one; spread 0.000 — the report barely separates the systems it reads
